newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Greece behind Cyprus missile row.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Greece behind Cyprus missile row.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller accused Greece on Friday of prompting the Cypriot government to create a missile crisis in the eastern Mediterranean.
"Greece is undoubtedly the country which holds most responsibility for this aggressive policy and which is encouraging, directing and supporting (Cyprus) on this path," Ciller told a news conference.
Turkey has threatened to knock out Cypriot anti-aircraft missiles to be bought from Russia if they are deployed on the island. The rockets could strike planes over mainland Turkey.
Ciller said fellow NATO-member Greece was using Cyprus as an instrument to foster its hostile policy against Ankara.
"Turkey cannot just look on as Greece brings Cyprus to the boil in the eastern Mediterranean, besieging it from the south and ruining the balances between the two countries," she said.

Relations between Ankara and Athens are traditionally strained and were put under further pressure a year ago in a military standoff over a deserted islet in the Aegean Sea. The two countries are also at odds over minority rights.
Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military junta then running Greece.
There are 30,000 Turkish troops in the northern third of Cyprus while the internationally-recognised Cyprus government controls the Greek Cypriot south.

The United States and Britain have urged Cyprus to cancel the Russian missile deal and Washington is to send an envoy to the island over the weekend to try and reduce the tension. Washington estimates the system will not be deployed for at least 16 months.
